severity_name: HEAVY SLOP WARNING — CRAFT INTEGRITY ADVISORY
headline: HEAVY SLOP WARNING: IMPOSSIBLE-PATTERN FRONT SETTLES OVER THE ETSY HOLLOWS AND PINTEREST SHALLOWS AS MACHINE-GENERATED CRAFT INSTRUCTIONS DIRECT HOBBYISTS TO CROCHET SHAPES THAT VIOLATE THE KNOWN GEOMETRY OF YARN
advisory: A slow-moving system of synthetic craft patterns has saturated the weekend leisure corridor, distributing downloadable PDFs that promise an adorable finished object and deliver forty rounds of instructions that terminate in a knot no human hand can complete. Residents are advised that a pattern instructing you to 'increase evenly while decreasing throughout' is not a challenge to your skill; it is a system that has never held a hook. The Service reminds crafters that a genuine designer's photograph shows the actual object, whereas a slop listing shows a rendered plush whose eyes are located inside its own head. Purchase with caution and count your stitches.

regional_outlook.conditions: Heavy accumulation of instant-download pattern PDFs, many priced to move and generated in bulk overnight. Storefronts display eleven hundred listings opened this week by a shop that joined yesterday.
Dense drifts of pin imagery showing crochet animals with the correct number of legs but the wrong number of everything else. Saving these boards is safe; attempting to make anything on them is not.

'Free amigurumi pattern' queries return synthetic tutorials with confident row counts corresponding to no achievable form. Expect fog around the phrase 'sew all pieces together as shown' where nothing is shown.
Craft-group waters rising as members post finished-object photos matching nothing that could arise from the attached instructions. Volunteer moderators reporting fatigue.
Low-content pattern anthologies washing ashore, each containing two hundred 'exclusive designs' and zero tested stitches. Cover art depicts objects the interior cannot produce.

specimen.status: Common and multiplying; peaks on weekends and rainy holidays.
specimen.habitat: Instant-download storefronts, pin boards, and any listing where the finished photo is suspiciously glossier than the craft.
specimen.field_marks: Instructions that command you to increase and decrease in the same round, a stitch count that changes with no cause, and a final assembly step reading 'attach remaining pieces' when no remaining pieces were ever made. The listing photo is a render, betrayed by symmetrical fur and a soul-absence in the eyes.
specimen.call: Round 14: sc in each st around (37 sts). Continue in pattern until piece measures desired length. Fasten off and weave in the magic.
specimen.confusion_species: Easily mistaken for a genuine indie designer's pattern, which also uses abbreviations and charts. Tell them apart by the reviews — real patterns accumulate photos of lopsided, loving, actually-completed objects; the slop specimen accumulates one-star notes reading 'this does not work' and a seller who never replies.

spotter_tip: Before you buy, look for a photo of the object being held by a human hand. Slop renders never include the hand — the pattern has no idea a hand exists, and neither does anything it has produced.
tomorrow: Craft-front weakens overnight; residual pattern debris lingers in bargain bins, with scattered impossible knitting moving in by evening.
